analysis.title: The Flow Show: Why save, why short, why risk-off
key_insights: BofA stays risk-off until rate hikes end or financial conditions ease. The triggers are oil (WTI below $70/bbl, described as underway), yields (GT10 below 4.5%, likely Dec-Jan) and a lower US dollar (currently moving the other way, peaks Feb-Mar).

Global tightening cycle (>70 rate hikes Jun'26-May'27) ends at the April FOMC at the earliest. The report says the US dollar surge and gold below $4k mean global liquidity is in retreat, and that CPI leaves no release valve for risk assets from lower UST yields despite oil down 15%.

Cyclicals point to downward revisions of 'boom' forecasts (5-6% nominal GDP, >15% EPS in '27): lumber -21%, metals -11%, blue-collar semis -26%. Consensus expects 18% S&P 500 EPS growth over the next 12 months.

Bull case: SPX above 8K, driven by buy-the-dip flows. Supports cited: equal-weighted S&P 500 back to highs, JNK, SPX, XBD and TSM holding at or above the 200dma, and a Trump-Xi-Putin meeting on Nov 18 at the Shenzhen APEC summit confirming 'peak oil'.

Bear case: SPX below 7K, from a US dollar spike and liquidity shortage, and a policy mistake as central banks hike into a slowdown. Higher credit spreads and lower stocks are described as the quickest way to end the K-shaped consumer and AI capex.

Most vulnerable to downside over the next 8 weeks: HY bonds, US and EM stocks, energy and healthcare, mega-cap consumer stocks. Most vulnerable to upside: gold, IG tech bonds, Japan and Europe stocks, China tech, small/mid-cap, semis, discretionary, homebuilders.

Weekly flows: $98.3bn to stocks (largest since Jun'26), $0.3bn to bonds, $49mm to gold, $1.9bn out of crypto, $17.9bn out of cash. US equities took $63.6bn in. Treasuries had a $0.6bn outflow, the first since Jun'26. EM debt had a 2-week outflow of $7.5bn, the largest since Jan'26.

Record year of inflows in '26: global equities $1.4tn annualized, US stocks $656bn, IG bonds $463bn, tech funds $222bn, Korea $78bn. The report says many investors are emotionally bearish but very few are short or underweight.

BofA Bull & Bear Indicator rose to 7.4 from 7.2 on strong equity inflows and narrower HY and subordinated bank spreads. The signal is Neutral. Equity Flow is at the 96th percentile and FMS Positioning at 100%. Global Stock Index Breadth is at 21% (Bearish).

Policy support for stocks: Taiwan announced a $15bn fund to support stocks, and Korea and China are making more 'Price Keeping Operation' moves. The report calls stock markets 'too big to fail' for global policymakers, which it gives as the reason no one shorts stocks.

US household equity wealth fell about $3tn in the past month but is up about $9tn in '26 and $19tn since Jan'25. Total US household equity wealth is about $74tn. The report cites consumption at 70% of GDP and a K-shaped consumer as reasons a recession is hard to get.

Inflation: the Oct NFIB survey showed the share of small businesses planning price hikes at the highest since Jul'22, historically consistent with at least 3-4% inflation. Feb'21 was the last month the Fed's 2% CPI target was met. Markets price rate hikes at the FOMC on Dec 9, Jan 27 and Mar 17.

Politics: 8 Senate seats flipped GOP to DEM in the midterms. The report says investors won't touch US Treasuries until they yield 5.5-6.5%. Michigan CDS showed no jump after the flip, but the share of small businesses naming taxes as the #1 problem is the highest since May'21.

Nov FMS is released Nov 17. 'Boom' expectations were 47% in Oct and cash was 3.9%. A big drop in 'boom' expectations and cash above 4.2% means sentiment is less of a headwind. 'Boom' staying high with cash below 3.7% means not enough fear to buy.

2026 YTD best trades: long oil-short crypto, long energy-short discretionary, long semis-short telecom, long small-cap value-short mega-cap growth, long Taiwan-short China, long cyber-short defense. The 25/25/25/25 portfolio of stocks, bonds, commodities and cash is annualizing 12%, the best since '21.
S&P 500 is on track for a 4th consecutive year of double-digit gains (13% annualized). Since 1871 that has happened only in 1942-45, 1949-52 and 1995-99.

BofA private clients hold $4.5tn AUM: 65.2% stocks (7-month low), 18.1% bonds, 9.5% cash. They had the biggest outflow from 2-10 year Treasury notes since Feb'26. Over 4 weeks they bought bank loan, TIPS and industrials ETFs and sold utilities, energy and consumer discretionary.
